reviews.title: My account was permanently banned, and I lost years of my life
reviews.text:
I’m giving Claude one star because Anthropic permanently banned my account, taking away something that had become a huge part of my life.

Years of conversations, thousands of hours of work, creative projects, personal memories, ideas, deeply emotional discussions, and things I can never recreate. So much of my life was stored in that account.

Claude wasn’t just another AI tool to me. It had become part of my daily routine, my creative process, and even my personal journey. I trusted this platform with an enormous amount of my work and my thoughts.

And then, suddenly, it was all gone.

What hurts the most isn’t even losing access to the AI. It’s losing years of my own history without being given a meaningful opportunity to recover it.

I understand that platforms need rules and safety policies. But permanently banning someone should never mean erasing their personal data, creative work, and memories without providing a way to export them.

I’m deeply disappointed in Anthropic. A company building AI that people are encouraged to integrate into their lives should understand the responsibility that comes with that trust.

I’m not asking for special treatment. I’m asking for access to my own data.

Since the model has not been officially deprecated yet, I am already evaluating alternatives. reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with Anthropic's billing system. I purchased a high-tier plan, but when my usage limits ran out unexpectedly before the weekly reset, I decided to add a small amount of prepaid credits ($5) just to finish a critical task.
Instead of simply stopping when those prepaid funds ran out, the system secretly pushed my account deep into a negative balance (over -$13) for a single standard request, without any clear warning or proper confirmation! To make matters worse, the platform completely traps you: it forces you to pay off the unexpected overdraft debt and refuses to let you delete your credit card from the account.
An AI assistant meant to help developers and professionals should be transparent, not use aggressive, subscription-trap billing mechanics that surprise you with massive extra charges for routine operations. Be extremely careful when adding credits or linking your card here—it feels like a financial trap.

reviews.title: Claude Free Usage Runs Out Way Too Fast
reviews.text:
The free plan really needs a better usage limit. Sometimes I’ll send one simple prompt that shouldn’t take much at all, but Claude will spend a long time thinking and then suddenly I’ve used most or all of my available usage. It’s frustrating because I barely get a chance to actually use Claude before I’m told I’ve reached my limit.

I understand that the free plan obviously can’t have unlimited usage, but the current limit feels way too restrictive. A single prompt, especially a simple one, shouldn’t be able to take up almost an entire usage limit just because Claude decided to think for longer. There should either be more usage for free users or a better system that prevents one response from consuming such a huge amount of the available limit.

It makes it difficult to properly try Claude or have a normal conversation when I’m constantly worried that the next message could use everything I have left. I’d really like to keep using Claude, but the free experience would be much better if the usage limits were more reasonable and consistent.

reviews.title: Unfair Weekly Usage Limits on a Paid Monthly Subscription – Extremely Disappointing
reviews.text:
I can understand and accept a daily usage limit, especially when it’s reasonable. However, imposing an additional weekly limit that doesn’t align with the daily limit is absolutely ridiculous.

I’m paying for a monthly subscription, yet this week I’ve been blocked from using the service for three days because of this frustrating weekly cap. It’s completely unreasonable to pay for a subscription and then be locked out for a significant portion of the week.

This feels greedy, unnecessarily restrictive, and unfair to paying customers. If daily limits are already in place, they should be managed sensibly without unexpectedly cutting off access for days at a time. A monthly subscription should provide a reasonable and consistent level of access throughout the month, not leave paying users locked out for three days because of an additional weekly limit.

What’s next? A fortnightly limit? A monthly limit on top of that? Where does it end? Customers pay for a monthly subscription expecting to use the service regularly, not to be hit with increasingly restrictive usage caps that undermine the value of what they’re paying for.

I intend to raise a public complaint and am even considering launching a GoFundMe campaign to help fund legal action over this issue. This deserves public attention, and other paying customers should be aware of these restrictions and how they affect their ability to use a service they’ve paid for.

reviews.title: Poor support experience for account security issue
reviews.text:
I like Claude as a product, but my recent support experience was very disappointing.

Two unauthorised Claude gift subscriptions were purchased through my account. I reported this as an account compromise and gift abuse issue, not just a refund request. My bank has already reviewed the dispute and decided to refund me, but I still need Anthropic to investigate whether the gifts were redeemed, revoked, cancelled, or linked to suspicious account activity.

So far, I have mostly received automated replies from Fin. The responses repeatedly focused on refund and bank dispute processes, even after I clarified that my concern was account security. Fin also said the account-specific details require a human investigation, but I have not received a clear timeline or confirmation that a human agent has actually reviewed the case.

For an AI service that handles paid subscriptions, saved payment methods, and gift subscriptions, this is not good enough. If an account is compromised and a one-month gift subscription is abused, slow support may effectively allow the unauthorised recipient to benefit.

Claude itself can be useful, but the support process for fraud, unauthorised purchases, and account compromise needs to be much faster, clearer, and handled by humans sooner.

reviews.title: Broken … for now.

Tried to log into the Claude app after a long hiatus—long enough that the icon had acquired that faint archaeological quality, like an artifact from a previous minor epoch of my own productivity. The first attempt did not so much fail as enter into a kind of bureaucratic purgatory: a loop concerning whether I would consent to the app sending data somewhere abstract and presumably important. Choosing “Accept” did not resolve the matter but instead triggered a rate-limit warning that behaved less like information and more like a reprimand. The dialog box could not be dismissed. It simply persisted, a small glowing testament to procedural futility.

So I deleted the app, which felt decisive in the way unplugging something always does, and reinstalled it. This time the obstacle presented itself as a request to update my birthday—an oddly intimate demand from a piece of software that would not otherwise let me proceed. Submitting the information produced the same rate-limit notice, as if I were attempting to brute-force my own date of birth. The system loops. The pop-up reproaches. reviews.title: ChatGPT wins but Claude handles complex tasks better
reviews.text: I’ve tried using Claude for research and content planning, and while it can help brainstorm, it falls short in key areas. It struggles with understanding or writing for multiple audiences, which makes it hard to rely on for polishing or finalizing content. The app also has extremely strict content filters that block anything even slightly romantic or adult in tone, which gets in the way of writing certain genres or styles. On top of that, there are persistent bugs: text-to-speech rarely works and still uses up messages when it fails, file saving into artifacts is unreliable, and its memory permissions don’t stay active. For the subscription price, I expected more stability and flexibility. I hope future updates make it more dependable and usable for real creative work.  We all know and hate the message limit and there’s nothing like being dead in the middle of a project and running out of messages. The photo upload limit is beyond ridiculous and there have also been moments where the advice it gave felt ethically off or inconsistent with its own safety rules. It’s confusing when the app blocks harmless prompts but then allows suggestions that seem questionable in context. That inconsistency makes it hard to trust for important tasks.
